checkpoint.prompt: What is the one-sentence frame this course runs on?
choices: Whatever we are to each other, we are one team for the child
Keep the peace at any cost
Win the important decisions

checkpoint.prompt: Being one team requires what, per this session?
choices: Being friends with the other parent
Agreeing on everything
Working the child's interests together, whatever the history between you

checkpoint.prompt: What does the child gain when the team holds?
choices: Two households pulling one direction, which lowers the load they carry
Fewer rules
A guarantee of no conflict

checkpoint.prompt: What does flooded mean in this session?
choices: Being sad
Your body so activated that judgment is gone; continuing makes it worse
Disagreeing strongly

checkpoint.prompt: What is the rule when you notice you are flooded?
choices: Push through to resolution
Pause, about twenty minutes, then resume
End all contact for the week
It is how long the body needs to actually come down; five minutes of silent rehearsing does not count
It is a rule of the platform
It gives you time to build your case

checkpoint.prompt: What are the three marks of businesslike communication here?
choices: Short, factual, about the child
Polite, warm, frequent
Written, formal, copied to others
Pickup Friday is 5:30 at school; she has her science fair board with her.
We need to talk about your choices lately.
Fine. Whatever works for you, as usual.

checkpoint.prompt: Why keep it to the child?
choices: Because the old disputes are settled
Because every message that stays on the child is one that cannot reopen the marriage
Because feelings are wrong

checkpoint.prompt: What buys back a co-parent's trust, per this session?
choices: Reliability, kept small promises, over time
A sincere conversation about the past
Generosity with money

checkpoint.prompt: How does this session treat court orders and agreements?
choices: As obstacles to work around when unfair
As the floor you never build against; trust is earned inside them, never against them
As relevant only to lawyers

checkpoint.prompt: Which is the right first promise to rebuild with?
choices: A large one, to prove commitment
A small one you are certain to keep, then another
None; let time do it

checkpoint.prompt: Who carries the distance between two homes, per this session?
choices: The parents equally
The child; your job is to lighten the load
Nobody, if the schedule is fair
Asking what happens at the other house
Letting the child feel free to love both homes out loud
Keeping the households completely identical

checkpoint.prompt: Your child praises something at the other home. The session's move is what?
choices: Receive it warmly; their ease is the win
Match it with something better at yours
Change the subject

checkpoint.prompt: What is the standard for handoffs in this session?
choices: Predictable beats perfect
Quick beats friendly
Flexible beats scheduled
The unresolved topic from last week
The child's things, the practical facts, a calm goodbye
A private word with the other parent about concerns

checkpoint.prompt: Why does predictability matter so much at the handoff moment?
choices: It saves time
The handoff is where the child feels the team most directly; calm sameness tells them the ground is solid
It prevents lateness

final_qa.prompt: Write the last message you sent the other parent, then rewrite it businesslike: short, factual, about the child. What changed?
Describe one flooded moment this course caught: where you felt it, how you paused, and what resuming later made possible.
Name the small promise you are using to rebuild trust inside the agreement that governs you, and your record of keeping it so far.
